label: first copy step after <DEL> when the echoed first token is k, long sequences (L>=6)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase at step L+1 (recall_idx == 1), the step where the model's first output, original token 0, is fed back as input, and essentially only when that token is k (first_tok == k; 99.8% of activation mass). It is silent for L <= 5 and active only for L = 6..9. Magnitude rises with L: L=6 carries 6% of mass and L=9 carries 39% with similar counts. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, on k at other positions, or at other recall indices. The rare activations with other first tokens (2, r, o, w) are tiny (about 0.01 of max).

issues: Minor, not systematic: all 184 test false positives are L=6 sequences (step 7). At L=6 precision is 0.93 and activations are weak (L=6 holds 6% of mass), so L=6 is a soft threshold where the feature is only starting to come on, not a sharp cutoff.

Minor: some of the 298 test misses (0.2% of mass) are recall_idx==1 steps where the first token is not k but orig(1)==k (e.g. '2 k x v ...' at 0.12 of max). As a rule this explains almost nothing: precision 0.010, mass recall 0.0014. Treat it as scattered noise.

Verified: there is zero activation in the original and delimiter phases and at any recall_idx other than 1. in_tok==k holds 99.8% of mass. L<=5 never fires. Mass share by L is 0.064/0.223/0.323/0.391 for L=6..9, which matches the explanation. Test F1 0.978 reproduces. Using L>=5 instead drops precision to 0.78.
